correctness.rationale: With probability Haar measure direct integration gives a_0=c²/(2π) and a_n=|1−e^{inc}|²/(2πn²) for n≠0. For p/q, the allowed nonconstant residue classes give uniform comparison with n⁻²; a missing Fourier coefficient is a continuous functional on C(T), and subtracting the atomic measures of two disjoint q-orbits annihilates all allowed modes. In the irrational case all frequencies are present, which gives uniform density by trigonometric polynomials and strict definiteness by uniqueness for finite measures. The O(n⁻²) upper bound and finite polynomials give continuous embedding in H¹ and density there; a sparse subsequence with summable n²a_n gives an H¹ member not in the RKHS by assigning coefficients √a_n. Testing single characters and then summing shows bounded inclusion iff inf (1+n²)^s a_n>0. The exponential difference is comparable to ||nα||, and the limsup formula for μ gives both strict regimes and the stated independent endpoint condition. Dividing in·f̂(n) by 1−e^{inc} gives the unique zero-mean transfer, and Parseval supplies exactly 2π and the separate constant term. The equation only sees the nonconstant part, so the claim is not restricted to mean-zero f. A single-character norm check and an exact q=3 orbit test were also verified. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; its finite diagnostics do not certify Diophantine asymptotics, and the description of two continued-fraction regimes overstates the script, which samples one badly approximable example. No expert or formal certification is asserted.
residual_risks: The claimed embedding endpoint is conditional on the uniform lower bound, not determined by the numerical irrationality exponent alone.
